paragraphs: Shabbetai son of R. Marinus. (A Yerushalmi, in the time of R. Chiyya.)[^1] In Bava Metzia 17 it is related that he promised his daughter-in-law a fine wool cloak in her marriage contract. Her marriage contract was lost. He said, ‘There was never any such obligation.’ Witnesses came—he said to them, ‘I paid it.’ He came before R. Chiyya, who told him, ‘You have been shown to have falsely denied the obligation concerning that cloak.’[^2]

From [Beitzah 32b](https://www.sefaria.org/Beitzah.32b.3), it appears that he was a distinguished man. It is related there that he came to Babylonia and asked them for business funding, but they did not give it to him; nor did they provide him with food. He said, ‘These people descend from the mixed multitude, for it is written: “He will grant you compassion and have compassion on you.” Whoever shows compassion to others is known to be descended from our father Abraham,’ etc.[^3]

notes.text: Hyman’s description ירושלמי is retained as Yerushalmi: it may denote a sage of the Land of Israel rather than specify the city of Jerusalem. The name follows the supplied proofread text, מרינוס; the older OCR reads מריגום and is not used to replace it.

The cloak is איצטלא דמלתא; the contract is her ketubah. Hyman gives Bava Metzia 17 without specifying a side of the folio. The earlier draft’s claim that איצטלא itself differed in the OCR was mistaken and is not retained.

The appraisal ‘it appears’ is Hyman’s inference. The statement about ancestry is Shabbetai’s reported rebuke, not an editorial assessment. The account and quotation were checked in the William Davidson edition, Beitzah 32b, paragraphs 3–4; the Bava Metzia passage was not independently checked.
